sources.disposition_reason: terms at https://abuse.ch/terms-of-use/ were read on 2026-11-07. §3.1 permits free access for not-for-profit purposes; §7.3 forbids derivative works without consent; AI-training is forbidden. Enabled for retrieval/local_storage/enrichment under the household not-for-profit condition, satisfied. commercial_use and derived_output and redistribution are refused: either conditional-not-satisfied (commercial requires a Spamhaus subscription) or prohibited outright (derived, redistribution). The abuse.ch Auth-Key is still required at retrieval time; a missing key is reported as a skip, not a failure, by scamwall fetch.
sources.privacy_implications: Records describe attacker infrastructure, not household activity. Bulk download only; no live query.
sources.intended_permitted_use: Local, non-commercial detection for one household.
sources.coverage_limitations: Malware distribution URLs only; not phishing or adware.
sources.operational_cost: Free under fair use for non-commercial; commercial API priced separately.

sources.classification_meaning: A certificate whose SAN resembles a protected brand. Signal: `suspicious`, never `harmful` on its own.
sources.disposition_reason: no terms citation was supplied for crt.sh; every grant stays `unknown` and the source stays disabled. brands.txt is empty, so even an enabled S6 would produce no signals. Owner step: read crt.sh terms, populate brands.txt, flip grants.
sources.privacy_implications: Records describe public certificate issuances; brand list is private to this host.
sources.intended_permitted_use: Local detection of domain impersonation of owner-listed brands.
sources.coverage_limitations: Depends entirely on the brands file. Produces suspicious signals, never block decisions on its own.
